impairment_notes.cause: Impairment is tested against recoverable amounts (value in use) from the independent valuer's DCF, so it tracks the valuation: (1) FY23: WACC rose from 7.7-8.0% (RBSA, Mar-22) to 9.01% (INMACS, Sep-22/Mar-23) after the valuer change and new WACC build (comparables beta, country-risk-adjusted ERP 9.08-9.73%, Kd 8.4-8.6%). The IM CFO blamed the 'huge rise in the global interest rate market' in 2022. Total EV fell from Rs 102,295 mn to Rs 85,458 mn, and NAV fell from 101.07 to 86.04. (2) FY24: small reversal as WACC eased to 8.85%/8.79% on lower ERP and Rf. (3) FY25: an H1 impairment (WACC up to 8.95%), then a large reversal at Mar-25 when WACC was cut to 8.00% through methodology changes (5-yr POWERGRID beta, 70:30 target leverage, AAA-based Kd), taking NAV to 94.12. (4) FY26: WACC held at 8.00%; standalone impairment of Rs 713.28 mn but consolidated PPE reversal of Rs 1,216.40 mn; NAV 90.79 (run-off). Management repeatedly calls it a non-cash entry with no impact on distributions.
